title: Grant (monaco compiler profile)
description: The compiled object naming what one agent cycle may write to, as produced by monaco's manifest-driven compile step. This is NOT the Field Kit's generic schema — see docs/kernel/GRANT.md "Monaco profile vs. the Field Kit Grant". A client-repo kit schema (.hexagen/grant.schema.json) requires only `paths` + `tools` as its core; `contexts` here is a monaco-specific extra that compiles into `paths`.

id.description: Stable identifier for this grant. A Trace record references the cycle it evidences by this id — it is never reconstructed after the fact from contexts/paths, which are not unique per grant.

principal.description: Who authorized this cycle — a human account, a CI policy name, an approval workflow id. Distinct from `agent`: the principal accepts responsibility for the grant existing; the agent is who executes under it.

agent.description: Which agent/tool identity this grant was issued to (an MCP client id, a CI job name, an editor-agent session id). A grant is issued to one agent identity, not a class of agents.

contexts.description: Manifest bounded-context names (manifest.yaml bounded_contexts[].name) this cycle may mutate. Monaco-specific: the compile step expands each entry into a `packages/<context>/` prefix in `paths` against this repo's manifest.yaml. A repo with no manifest to compile against (the Field Kit's general case) omits this field entirely — `paths` is what every enforcement point actually checks, `contexts` is only how monaco fills it in.

paths.description: Workspace-relative path prefixes this cycle may write to. The one field every enforcement point checks, on any profile. For a monaco-compiled grant: `packages/<context>/` for each entry in `contexts`, plus any caller-supplied extras — extras are listed here for a human to review (`hexagen grant show`), never compiled from a guess, and `check` applies the same prefix rule to them as to the context-derived entries.

tools.description: Which write tools this cycle may invoke — the seven MCP mutation tool names today, an editor-write capability id or a shell-write id once that adapter exists. `paths` alone is not sufficient: a grant naming the right path but not the tool that would use it still denies that tool. This is what makes a grant a scope on *actions*, not only on *locations*.

mode.description: "propose" grants may only create a Transaction (reach hexagen_create_context / add_dependency / etc., never hexagen_accept_transaction); "write" grants may also accept. This is the difference between an agent that may draft a change and one that may land it — independent of which contexts/paths/tools it's scoped to.

max_files.description: Optional cap on distinct files touched in one cycle, independent of path scope — a blast-radius limit even within an otherwise-legitimate path.

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp. Required even though v1 always mints a fresh grant per cycle and discards it immediately after: "discarded per cycle" is a usage policy this slice follows, not a reason to omit the field a persistent grant store will need on day one.

revoked_at.description: Set when a grant is revoked before its natural expiry (a human pulls it mid-cycle). Absent on an active, unrevoked grant.

signature.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) over every field above except this one, keyed by the trust root at .hexagen/grant-signing.key (see docs/kernel/GRANT.md "Enforcement point"). Not in `required`: a grant without one is syntactically valid but is denied at accept time all the same, since an unsigned or wrongly-signed grant is never trusted as authorization, whatever its other fields claim.
